sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's learn how to create methods in Java - your code's superheroes! Methods help you organize and reuse code like LEGO blocks.

• What methods are and why they're useful
• How to define your own methods
• The basic structure of a method
• How to call methods to make them work

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine methods as little robots that do specific jobs for you. Need to calculate something? There's a robot for that. Need to display a message? Another robot!

Methods are like these robots - they:
• Have a specific job to do
• Can be called whenever you need that job done
• Can take inputs and give outputs

Here's the simplest method structure:
```java
public static void methodName() {
    // Code to execute
}
```
• `public static` - We'll learn these later (just include them for now)
• `void` - Means the method doesn't return anything
• `methodName()` - Your custom name for the method
• `{}` - The method's code goes between these braces

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: A method definition includes modifiers, return type, name, parameter list, and body
The return type specifies the type of value the method returns (void if none)
Parameters are variables declared in the method header that receive argument values
The method name should describe what the method does using camelCase
A return statement sends a value back to the caller and exits the method

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Methods are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks. Every method has a name, body, and can be called when needed. Practice defining and calling simple methods to build confidence.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct method definition in Java?
options: int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
int add(a, b) { return a + b; }
method add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
questions.explanation: A method definition requires a return type, method name, and parameter list with types. 'int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }' is the correct syntax.

questions.question: What does the 'return type' in a method signature specify?
options: The type of value the method sends back to the caller
The access level of the method
questions.explanation: The return type specifies what type of value the method returns to the caller. If a method returns no value, its return type is 'void'.
